description: Ed25519 signatures on which implementations disagree. `valid` is the verdict of Kern (docs/hybrid-signatures.md, section 2.5). `lenient` is the verdict of a verifier that makes only the checks RFC 8032 requires and compares the bytes of R.

cases.name: honest
cases.comment: An ordinary signature.

cases.name: honest, another message
cases.comment: An ordinary signature, checked against another message.

cases.name: S plus the group order
cases.comment: The scalar S of a valid signature replaced by S + L: the same value modulo the group order, another encoding.

cases.name: S with the top bits set
cases.comment: The scalar S of a valid signature with its three top bits set.

cases.name: public key of order 1 (canonical), R of order 1, S zero
cases.comment: Nobody holds a secret for this key. [S]B = R + [k]A holds because everything lies in the small subgroup.

cases.name: public key of order 1 (sign bit set although x is 0), R of order 1, S zero
cases.comment: Nobody holds a secret for this key. [S]B = R + [k]A holds because everything lies in the small subgroup.

cases.name: public key of order 1 (y written as y + p), R of order 1, S zero
cases.comment: Nobody holds a secret for this key. [S]B = R + [k]A holds because everything lies in the small subgroup.

cases.comment: Nobody holds a secret for this key. [S]B = R + [k]A holds because everything lies in the small subgroup.

cases.name: honest key, R is the identity
cases.comment: Made by the key holder with the nonce 0. [S]B = R + [k]A holds exactly, and S / k is the secret scalar: such a signature gives the key away.

cases.name: honest key, R is the identity written as p + 1
cases.comment: The same with the identity encoded as y = p + 1.

cases.name: honest key, R is the identity with the sign bit set
cases.comment: The same with the sign bit set although x is 0.

cases.name: honest key, R of order 8
cases.comment: 8[S]B = 8R + 8[k]A holds, [S]B = R + [k]A does not.

cases.name: public key of mixed order, challenge multiple of 8
cases.comment: The key is an ordinary key plus a point of order 8. [S]B = R + [k]A holds because [k] cancels the small part, but the key is not in the subgroup of prime order.

cases.name: public key of mixed order, challenge not multiple of 8
cases.comment: 8[S]B = 8R + 8[k]A holds, [S]B = R + [k]A does not.

cases.name: honest key, R of mixed order
cases.comment: 8[S]B = 8R + 8[k]A holds, [S]B = R + [k]A does not.

cases.name: public key and R of mixed order, small parts cancel
cases.comment: [S]B = R + [k]A holds exactly, with a key and a nonce point that both carry a point of small order: neither is in the subgroup of prime order.

cases.name: public key written as y + p (y = 3), ordinary signature bytes
cases.comment: An encoding that is not canonical, of a point nobody holds a secret for.

cases.name: public key of 31 bytes
cases.comment: Truncated public key.

cases.name: public key of 33 bytes
cases.comment: Public key with one more byte.

cases.name: signature of 63 bytes
cases.comment: Truncated signature.

cases.name: signature of 65 bytes
cases.comment: Signature with one more byte.

cases.name: public key that is not a point
cases.comment: No point of the curve has y = 2.

public_keys_rule: Public keys under rule 2 of section 2.5 alone, the check made when a key is recorded: `valid` says whether the 32 bytes are the canonical encoding of a point of the subgroup of prime order, other than the identity. Added after the freeze of the profile, for a rule that exists: the cases above are unchanged.
